command:
set -euo pipefail
cd /tmp

echo "== verify staged inputs against their pinned sha256 (same proteome + queries as blast) =="
{ printf '%s  %s\n' 9b43da92651b35814597af6a8b18f500b768679a49fa4678224f384917ce7668 ensembl116_pep.fa.gz
  printf '%s  %s\n' 6b43cff7568a5dead256262b159fe4b1d7fd7f97128efbcc8613d4dbedaacfa9 queries20.fa
} > pins.sha256
sha256sum -c pins.sha256

# diamond makedb reads plain FASTA; gzip is a base-image utility, not a second tool
# (both steps here are diamond).
gzip -dc ensembl116_pep.fa.gz > pep.fa

echo "== diamond makedb: Ensembl 116 human proteome =="
diamond makedb --in pep.fa -d pepdb 2> makedb.log

echo "== diamond blastp --very-sensitive: 20 queries vs the whole proteome =="
# --very-sensitive puts diamond in a sensitivity regime comparable to blastp's default.
# Comparing diamond's DEFAULT (fast) mode against blastp would be the like-with-like trap:
# different sensitivity modes return different hit sets for reasons unrelated to correctness
# (the same error as bowtie2 end-to-end vs --local). Match the modes, then compare.
diamond blastp -q queries20.fa -d pepdb \
  --outfmt 6 qseqid sseqid pident length qlen evalue bitscore \
  --very-sensitive --max-target-seqs 20 -p 4 -o dmnd_hits.tsv 2> blastp.log

# ---- smoke check ----
# The 20 queries ARE the first 20 records of the database (blast's self-hit design), so each
# must find itself: full-length, 100% identity, nothing beating it on bitscore. Algorithmic,
# so exact assertions -- the diamond analog of blast's self-hit identity.
#
# CROSS-CODE, applying \"compare like with like\": the naive metric -- does diamond's #1
# subject per query equal blast's #1 -- gives 1/20 here, NOT because the tools disagree but
# because these first-20 proteins are near-identical paralogs whose self-hit TIES on bitscore
# with a paralog (measured: 19/20 are exact ties, 0 real losses), and each tool breaks the
# tie by its own arbitrary order. That is blast's own documented caveat (\"nothing beats
# itself\", not \"self is first\"). So the asserted cross-code claim is tie-agnostic and
# score-agnostic (diamond's heuristic bitscores differ from blastp's by design): BOTH tools
# recover all 20 full-length 100% self-hits with none beaten -- the shared algorithmic truth.
selfstats() { awk -F'\t' '
  $1==$2 && $3==100 && $4==$5 {self[$1]=$7}
  {if($1!=$2 && $7>other[$1])other[$1]=$7}
  END{ s=0; b=0; for(q in self){s++; if((q in other)&&other[q]>self[q])b++} print s" "b }' "$1"; }
DST=$(selfstats dmnd_hits.tsv); DSELF=${DST%% *}; DBEATEN=${DST##* }
BST=$(selfstats blast_hits.tsv); BSELF=${BST%% *}; BBEATEN=${BST##* }
DQH=$(cut -f1 dmnd_hits.tsv | sort -u | wc -l | tr -d ' ')

{
  echo "diamond_self_hits    $DSELF   want exactly 20   (full-length, 100% identity)"
  echo "diamond_self_beaten  $DBEATEN   want exactly 0    (nothing outscores a self-hit)"
  echo "diamond_queries_hit  $DQH   want exactly 20"
  echo "blast_self_hits      $BSELF   want exactly 20   (cross-code: blast recovers the same self-hits)"
  echo "blast_self_beaten    $BBEATEN   want exactly 0    (cross-code: unbeaten in blast too)"
} > smoke-check.txt
cat smoke-check.txt

test "$DSELF"   -eq 20
test "$DBEATEN" -eq 0
test "$DQH"     -eq 20
test "$BSELF"   -eq 20
test "$BBEATEN" -eq 0
echo "SMOKE CHECK PASSED"
